Since 2020, the population of children under 5 in large urban counties has dropped 7%. 

In NYC, that number is 18%. 

Liena Zagare discusses a new @ManhattanInst report from her and @cojobrien that identifies a four-pillar policy agenda to reverse the urban family exodus.

Video
Read the full report here: manhattan.institute/article/…

American cities cannot take families for granted. Their departure from our urban centers is an early indicator of decline.

To feel welcomed and wanted in cities, families need:
- Family-friendly housing
- Desirable childcare
- High-quality schools
- Safety

Families choosing large cities over suburban communities pay a higher share of their income for center-based child-care arrangements. In a typical large urban county, the median family will pay nearly 16% of its income for infant child care, compared with less than 13% in suburban communities.

Families prefer to trade common space for additional bedrooms. But because of regulatory barriers, housing that fits families is scarce.

Average 3-bedroom home prices in large urban counties have risen 60% since 2000. In NYC, only 19% of rental apartments have 3+ bedrooms.

Families are fleeing to the suburbs, but it isn’t just out-migration. Birthrates are a huge part of the story.

In large urban counties, birthrates are down 18% since 2010—more than twice the national rate of decline. The denser the city, the faster fertility is falling.

Between early 2020 and mid-2024, the population of children under five years old declined by 7% in large urban counties—more than twice the nationwide rate of decline.

Since the spring of 2020, the number of young children has fallen about 19% in New York; 16% in Cook County, Illinois; 15% in San Francisco; and 14% in Los Angeles County.

Losing families in large numbers is a sign that your city is in decline. Unfortunately, that's exactly what's happening in American cities—and it's not just a pandemic blip.

New @ManhattanInst research by @cojobrien and Liena Zagare diagnoses the urban family exodus and lays out the agenda for reversing it. 🧵
